subject: Marketplace private-offer: unit-price sensitivity & next steps
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Jared Myers <procurement@acme-data.com>, AWS Marketplace <aws-marketplace@amazon.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 17:12:00 -0800
Subject: Marketplace private-offer: unit-price sensitivity & next steps

Hi Jared / AWS team —

Thanks again for the discovery earlier today. Quick recap and the asks I promised:

Key points from the call:
- ACME's primary workload: document ingestion + retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for customer support.
- Expected production traffic: 8–12B tokens/month in steady state (spikes to ~15B).
- Peak request latency SLOs: 200–350ms per short-chat request.
- Procurement preference: AWS Marketplace private offer if the unit economics can be mapped to their internal chargeback.

What I need to confirm from you (Jared):
1) Target total monthly budget range for Redwood inference licensing (list or private-offer price) — you mentioned a notional $/month range on the call; can you confirm a target $/1M tokens?
2) Any internal marketplace constraints: pricing cadence, PO timing, or specific invoice workflow required by your billing team?
3) Whether ACME can accept a gated canary (dedicated pool) for weeks 1–4 during rollout.

From Redwood side we will:
- Draft a marketplace private-offer mapping that shows list price, marketplace fee assumptions, and the equivalent private-offer unit price to hit three target $/1M thresholds (conservative / target / aggressive).
- Attach a lightweight MPO-pricing-template.xlsx showing how we map tokens -> invoice line items and sample monthly cost at different tiers.

Next steps / ask: please reply with the confirmed target $/1M tokens (or budget band) and any billing constraints so we can finalize the private-offer numbers.

Thanks —
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[e] evelyn.hart@redwood.com | [m] +1 (415) 555-0189

Attachment: MPO-pricing-template.xlsx (pricing mapping template)

From: Jared Myers <procurement@acme-data.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, AWS Marketplace <aws-marketplace@amazon.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Feb 2027 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Marketplace private-offer: unit-price sensitivity & next steps

Evelyn —

Thanks for the clear notes. Quick answers from ACME procurement / billing:

1) Target economics: our budget owners are looking for an effective price in the $300–$420 per 1M tokens range (USD) for production traffic. The preferred target point to get internal approval is ~$350 / 1M tokens.
2) Marketplace constraints: we prefer private-offer flow through AWS so spend shows up on our monthly AWS invoice. The procurement team requires the private-offer PO to reference our internal cost center (CC-7732) and requires net-30 payment terms.
3) Canary: acceptable, but we will require a short SOW addendum (1 page) that states rollback conditions.

For clarity: those $/1M numbers need to account for the AWS marketplace seller fee (we expect seller side fee and any pass-through to buyer to be clear in the offer). If you can show list price -> marketplace discount -> final per-1M effective price that'd be ideal.

Cc'd billing@acme-data.com to confirm the cost center flow.

Jared Myers
Head of Procurement | ACME Data
procurement@acme-data.com

On Sun, Feb 21, 2027 at 08:40 AM AWS Marketplace <aws-marketplace@amazon.com> wrote:
> Hi all — happy to coordinate the private offer. We typically accept seller-provided unit mapping in a spreadsheet and will ingest the offer once buyer signs. Seller fees are documented here: https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/seller-fees
> 
> - AWS MP team

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Jared Myers <procurement@acme-data.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 10:01:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Marketplace private-offer: unit-price sensitivity & next steps

Eve / Dev —

I ran the numbers with the volumes Jared provided. High-level mapping and assumptions below so we can produce the MPO spreadsheet for AWS:

Assumptions:
- Steady-state tokens/month: 10B (midpoint of 8–12B).
- Target effective price: $350 / 1M tokens (customer stated preference).
- AWS marketplace seller fee (assumed for planning): 5% of seller revenue (we'll confirm exact % with AWS MP).
- Redwood target gross margin on MPO revenue (post-fee) target: ~40% on incremental hosted inference revenue.

Calculations (rounded):
- Customer wants $350 per 1M tokens. For 10B tokens that's 10,000 * $350 = $3,500,000/month.
- If seller fee is 5%, seller gross receipts = $3,500,000 / (1 - 0.05) ≈ $3,684,211 list price on AWS marketplace.
- Our net after fee = $3,500,000, and to hit ~40% gross margin we need cost of goods sold (infra + ops) ~ $2,100,000, which implies our blended unit cost ~ $210 / 1M tokens. That lines up with current dedicated pool TCO estimates assuming quantized weights and batching.

Price table we should surface in MPO spreadsheet (list -> post-fee -> effective):
- Aggressive: list = $3,000 / 1M -> post-fee ~ $2,850 -> effective to buyer $2,850 (not relevant here, example only)
- Target: list ≈ $368.42 / 1M -> post-fee ≈ $350 / 1M -> buyer sees $350 / 1M
- Conservative (higher buyer price): list ≈ $442.11 / 1M -> post-fee ≈ $420 / 1M

Action items for the MPO template:
- Column for list price per 1M token (what we submit to AWS).
- Column for assumed marketplace fee %.
- Column for effective buyer price / 1M tokens.
- Monthly extrapolation rows (1B, 5B, 10B, 15B).
- Include a row showing expected Redwood gross margin at each price point under current infra estimates.

Eve — happy to draft the MPO-pricing-template.xlsx. Dev, can you validate the infra cost assumptions quickly so we don't over/under commit on margin?

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, GTM Revenue | Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Jared Myers <procurement@acme-data.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Marketplace private-offer: unit-price sensitivity & next steps

Thanks everyone — consolidated next steps and deliverables below:

1) Redwood deliverable (due Wed 24 Feb): final MPO-pricing-template.xlsx populated with three price bands (conservative / target / aggressive), seller-fee assumptions, and monthly cost tables for 1B / 5B / 10B / 15B tokens. (Ben to own numbers, Dev to validate infra cost row.)
2) ACME deliverable: confirm the $350 / 1M target (Jared) and confirm acceptance of AWS private-offer flow + net-30 PO + CC-7732 reference. (Jared to confirm by EOD Wed 24 Feb).
3) AWS MP: confirm the seller fee % and preferred ingestion format for the MPO spreadsheet. (AWS MP to confirm by Wed 24 Feb).
4) Legal / SOW: procurement will provide a 1-page SOW addendum template for the canary; Redwood to accept or propose edits.

I attached the MPO-pricing-template.xlsx and a quick token-volume-breakdown.csv that maps their stated traffic patterns to monthly tokens. Ben / Dev — let me know if anything in the calculations above needs to move before I push the MPO to AWS.

If we get confirmations by Wed we can have a private-offer draft ready for ACME to ingest in AWS and for their billing team to reference in the PO.

Best —
Evelyn
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: MPO-pricing-template.xlsx, token-volume-breakdown.csv
